title: Gandouling inhibits hepatic fibrosis in Wilson's disease through Wnt-1/beta-catenin signaling pathway.
authors: Cheng, Chenglong; Wang, Qiang; Huang, Yurong; Xue, Qiuyun; Wang, Yuting; Wu, Peng; Liao, Faxue; Miao, Chenggui
one_liner_zh: 研究中药肝豆灵通过Wnt-1/β-catenin通路抑制Wilson病肝纤维化，涉及分子对接但非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGIC SIGNIFICANCE: Wilson's disease (WD) hepatic fibrosis is the result of chronic liver injury induced by Cu(2+) deposition in the liver. Gandouling (GDL) is a hospital preparation of the First Affiliated Hospital of Anhui University of Chinese Medicine. Previous studies have found that GDL can play an anti-inflammatory, anti-oxidation, and promote Cu(2+) excretion, which has a clear anti-WD effect. AIM OF THE STUDY: We found that Wnt-1 was significantly up-regulated in the liver tissue of toxic-milk (TX) mouse in the WD gene mutant model, and the monomer components of GDL could combine well with Wnt-1. Therefore, in this work, we used RT-qPCR, Western blot, immunofluorescence, network pharmacology, molecular docking, and related methods to study the effects of GDL on hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation and Wnt-1/beta-catenin pathway in TX mice to clarify the effect of GDL on WD hepatic fibrosis. RESULTS: GDL could alleviate hepatic fibrosis, improve liver function, and inhibit the activation of HSC in TX mice. Network pharmacology predicted that the Wnt-1/beta-catenin was the target of GDL, and molecular dynamics further revealed that GDL has a good binding ability with Wnt-1 and inhibits the Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway through Wnt-1. Furthermore, we found that GDL blocked the Wnt-1/beta-catenin signaling pathway in the liver of TX mice in vivo. In vitro, serum containing GDL blocked the Cu(2+) ion-induced Wnt-1/beta-catenin signaling pathway in LX-2 cells. Therefore, GDL blocked the Wnt-1/beta-catenin signaling pathway, inhibited HSC activation, and improved WD hepatic fibrosis by binding to Wnt-1. CONCLUSION: GDL improves hepatic fibrosis in WD model mice by blocking the Wnt-1/beta-catenin signaling pathway, and Wnt-1 may be a new target for the diagnosis and treatment of WD. This reveals a new mechanism of GDL against WD, and promotes the clinical promotion of GDL.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学意义：威尔逊病（Wilson's disease, WD）肝纤维化是肝脏中Cu(2+)沉积引起的慢性肝损伤的结果。肝豆灵（Gandouling, GDL）是安徽中医药大学第一附属医院的院内制剂。既往研究发现，GDL具有抗炎、抗氧化及促进Cu(2+)排泄的作用，并表现出明确的抗WD效果。研究目的：我们发现，在WD基因突变模型毒奶（toxic-milk, TX）小鼠的肝组织中，Wnt-1显著上调，且GDL的单体成分能与Wnt-1良好结合。因此，在本研究中，我们采用RT-qPCR、Western blot、免疫荧光、网络药理学、分子对接及相关方法，研究GDL对TX小鼠肝星状细胞（hepatic stellate cell, HSC）活化及Wnt-1/beta-catenin通路的影响，以阐明GDL对WD肝纤维化的作用。结果：GDL能减轻TX小鼠的肝纤维化，改善肝功能，并抑制HSC的活化。网络药理学预测Wnt-1/beta-catenin为GDL的作用靶点，分子动力学进一步揭示GDL与Wnt-1具有良好的结合能力，并通过Wnt-1抑制Wnt/beta-catenin信号通路。此外，我们发现在体内，GDL阻断了TX小鼠肝脏中的Wnt-1/beta-catenin信号通路。在体外，含GDL的血清阻断了LX-2细胞中Cu(2+)离子诱导的Wnt-1/beta-catenin信号通路。因此，GDL通过结合Wnt-1阻断Wnt-1/beta-catenin信号通路，抑制HSC活化，并改善WD肝纤维化。结论：GDL通过阻断Wnt-1/beta-catenin信号通路改善WD模型小鼠的肝纤维化，且Wnt-1可能是WD诊断和治疗的新靶点。这揭示了GDL抗WD的新机制，并促进了GDL的临床推广。
